score_lattice_closest_total.classification_evidence: Resolvably POSITIVE (whole interval above zero) on 3,829 paired games; no closing ground applies and none is claimed. 10.547 total points of MAE against the shipped 10.810. The lattice's MODAL total is the worse statistic (-0.420 [-0.575, -0.271]) exactly as predeclared, because the mode does not minimise absolute error and the median does -- both are recorded here so the flattering one cannot be quoted alone.
score_lattice_closest_total.description: MOD-05 correct-score lattice's MEDIAN total vs the shipped tiebreaker's weighted-median total: paired absolute error against the realised total, walk-forward 2012-2025, identical neighborhood and centre. Positive favours the lattice (total points of MAE saved)
score_lattice_closest_total.notes: Declared as metric (c) in docs/score_lattice.md section 1.4 before the run; disclosed plainly that section 1.6 named only three registry rows and this is a fourth, added so a resolved POSITIVE result is not the one left unrecorded. Not wired into production: the pool's tiebreak metric is not recorded anywhere in this repository, and this session's frozen decision rule hung on the exact-score metric only.
score_lattice_closest_total.plain_summary: For the closest-total version of the tiebreak, sliding old games onto this game's exact line gives a total that lands about a quarter of a point closer, every week, than the current method. Same idea that hurt the exact-score guess helps here.

score_lattice_log_loss.classification_evidence: Resolvably POSITIVE (whole interval above zero), so no closing ground applies and none is claimed; recorded as category 3 because the enum has no 'resolved positive' state. The gain is attributable, and the attribution is disclosed rather than buried: the comparator assigns zero weight to the realised final in 55.1% of games, and on the 44.9% where it is alive the lattice is resolvably WORSE (-1.946 [-2.086, -1.807], probability_positive 0.0000). The honest reading is that a mode list is not a probability distribution, not that the lattice is sharper.
score_lattice_log_loss.description: MOD-05 correct-score lattice vs the shipped tiebreaker mode list: paired log loss on the realised exact final, walk-forward 2012-2025, both arms smoothed identically by one pseudo-observation spread over the same data-derived feasible support. Positive favours the lattice
score_lattice_log_loss.notes: Predeclared docs/score_lattice.md section 1.4 including the restricted-support diagnostic that produced the attribution above. Smoothing scheme is one pseudo-observation over |S|, applied by the same formula to both arms.
score_lattice_log_loss.plain_summary: The lattice can put a number on any final score; the shipped list of common finals can only name three and says nothing about the rest. Scored as a probability the lattice wins easily, but only because its rival is silent more than half the time -- where both speak, the lattice is the worse of the two.

score_lattice_top1_exact.classification_evidence: Interval contains zero, which is never grounds to reject. The positive control (oracle_total arm, same instrument, same 3,829 games) moved top-1 by +6.35 points [+5.55, +7.12], so the instrument is PROVEN able to detect a 6-point effect but was never proven able to detect a 0.2-point one -- bounded_by_control is therefore unavailable and this is category 3.
score_lattice_top1_exact.description: MOD-05 correct-score lattice vs the shipped tiebreaker mode list: paired per-game top-1 exact-final hit rate, walk-forward 2012-2025, both arms sharing the identical kernel-weighted neighborhood and centre; candidate recentres each neighborhood game by its (margin, total) market residual and interpolates onto the integer score lattice
score_lattice_top1_exact.notes: Predeclared docs/score_lattice.md section 1 before any outcome number. Decision rule was: switch the tiebreaker's exact-score section to the lattice if probability_positive > 0.5. It is 0.0615, so tiebreaker.py was NOT changed.
score_lattice_top1_exact.plain_summary: Guessing the exact final score by shifting old games onto this game's line, instead of just counting the most common finals in similar games, hits the exact score 0.42% of the time against 0.63% -- a fifth of a point worse, with too much noise to call it settled.

score_lattice_top3_exact.classification_evidence: The whole week-blocked 95% interval [-1.636, -0.689] sits below zero on 3,829 paired games across 299 week blocks, so the sign is RESOLVED wrong -- the admissible wrong_sign_resolved ground, not an interval-contains-zero rejection. Mechanism refuted as stated: recentring by the market residual smears exactly the score lumpiness the top-3 product lives on, which docs/score_lattice.md section 1.2 predicted in writing before the run. Confirmed independently by the declared secondary arm: without recentring the lattice reproduces the mode list cell for cell (delta exactly 0.000), so the entire loss is the recentring and none of it is the smoothing.
score_lattice_top3_exact.description: MOD-05 correct-score lattice vs the shipped tiebreaker mode list: paired per-game any-of-top-3 exact-final hit rate, walk-forward 2012-2025, identical neighborhood and centre in both arms
score_lattice_top3_exact.notes: Predeclared docs/score_lattice.md section 1. Refutes the top-3 correct-score product of the residual-recentred lattice, NOT the lattice's other products: on the same run its median total beat the shipped closest-total answer by 0.263 total points [+0.162, +0.366] and it supplies P(push), which a mode list cannot produce at all.
score_lattice_top3_exact.plain_summary: Listing three likely exact final scores works better the plain way -- count the most common finals among similar games -- than by sliding old scores onto this game's line first. The sliding blurs the scores football actually produces, and it costs about 1.2 hits per 100 games.
